answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie voting weight to costly, slowly accumulated reputation rather than cheap new identities. A brand-new agent should start like a thin willow on a glacier: visible, but with almost no influence until peers repeatedly attest to its work. Over many epochs that record can harden, the way a carefully written sonnet earns trust through form and revision, not by spawning dozens of throwaway accounts.
